match_note: The figures and claims the referees cite match arXiv v1. Examples: peak position unchanged up to 3.5 mJ/cm2 in Fig. 2h; UED H-broadening read as topological defects; I1/I2 amplitude–phase decomposition in Fig. 3; Fig. 4h real-space schematic; Fig. 3b,d,e; the line about the bilayer CDW being undetectable in UED; Bragg Debye-Waller comparison. There are minor differences. The submitted title ('Dynamics of a jointly commensurate moiré charge density wave') differs from the v1 title. Reference numbering is shifted: the YBCO/Cr references the referee calls 34–36 are refs 31–33 in v1. Ref. 4 is cited as Nat. Mater. in the reviewed version but as arXiv in v1. The figure numbers R1 cites ('Fig. 1a and 1g') correspond to v1 Fig. 2a/2g, as the authors' reply confirms. Supplementary figure numbering (e.g. 'Fig. S7') cannot be checked against v1.

concerns.quote: The presentation repeatedly switches between experimental techniques (time-resolved x-ray diffraction, electron diffraction, ARPES, and back to x-ray diffraction) and between measurements at q and q′ without a clear logical progression.
concerns.summary: The manuscript jumps between techniques and wavevectors without a clear narrative and should be reorganized by physical question.

concerns.quote: inspection of the CDW peaks in Fig. 1a and Fig. 1g suggests markedly different levels of suppression: approximately 20% in one case and nearly 40% in the other.
concerns.summary: The intensity suppression differs inconsistently between the tr-XRD and UED peak profiles, suggesting normalization, pump–probe volume or penetration-depth problems.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: Such behavior can arise from many types of structural disorder, including dislocations, domain walls, strain gradients, or conventional defects.
concerns.summary: Anisotropic peak broadening only implies anisotropic correlation lengths and could come from ordinary structural disorder rather than CDW-specific defects.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: The manuscript does not provide evidence that uniquely identifies the defects as topological. (R1) / The topological scenario strikes me as naive. (R2)
concerns.summary: The 'topological' label is unjustified: there is no scaling or KTHNY-type analysis (R1), and true topological defects should be stable, whereas the response here is reversible (R2).

concerns.quote: Since diffraction measures the intensity of the scattered wave (the modulus squared of the structure factor), the phase information of the order parameter is not directly accessible.
concerns.summary: It is unclear how intensity-only diffraction can separate amplitude and phase dynamics, so the I1/I2 decomposition needs clearer justification or reformulation.

concerns.quote: with Electron diffraction the Q-resolution is weak. Could you estimate the Q-resolution obtained in your electron diffraction experiment
concerns.summary: The UED momentum resolution must be quantified to support the claimed absence of peak shifts and the measured width changes.

concerns.quote: In more unidirectional systems (NbSe3, for example), the correlation lengths are always significantly larger in the directions transverse to the chains... Your observation of the broadening as a function of H is not surprising.
concerns.summary: Transverse-dominant broadening is generic in anisotropic (t vs t') CDW systems, so it is not evidence for a special defect type.

concerns.quote: the increase in transverse width may also be due to a simple curvature of the wavefronts without affecting the wavelength.
concerns.summary: Transverse broadening could come from CDW wavefront curvature, pinned at sample surfaces or at grain edges (with domain coarsening); the referee also asks about the sample surface and thickness effects.

concerns.quote: the representation in real space of the topological defects you show (FIG 4 h) would imply a tilt in the QCDW vector, which is not the case here.
concerns.summary: The real-space defect schematic implies a tilt of the CDW wavevector, which the data do not show.

concerns.quote: In CDW systems, Bragg reflections are much less sensitive to temperature compared to CDW satellites. How do satellites vary with temperature compared to Bragg reflections in EuTe4 ?
concerns.summary: The Bragg peak drop (~15%) is large relative to the satellite drop (~30%), raising the question of whether thermal effects contribute to the CDW dynamics; static temperature dependence is requested.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: Don’t your time-resolved studies ultimately show that you are observing a single object, rather than the coexistence of two distinct waves that interact?
concerns.summary: The similar q and 2q behaviour seems to contradict a picture of two independent coexisting CDWs, suggesting a single coupled object.

concerns.quote: Perhaps you could mention the work on NbSe3 in the low temperature phase with the two coexisting (non-parallel) CDWs where a clear echo between the two CDWs is observed
concerns.summary: The referee suggests discussing Ayari et al. (PRL 2004) on coupled coexisting CDWs in NbSe3; v1 already cites it as ref. 8, but only for the definition of joint commensuration.

concerns.quote: it is difficult to accept this paper for publication unless the ref 4 has been published.
concerns.summary: The work relies on the unpublished, incompletely cited Ref. 4 establishing the moiré CDW in EuTe4.

concerns.quote: Refrence 34, 35 and 36 do not deal with CDW in RTe3 systems but in either YBaCuO or Chromium.
concerns.summary: Several references are miscited as RTe3 CDW work when they concern YBCO or chromium.

concerns.quote: Fig.3D : Is there a color error in the legend?
concerns.summary: The fluence colours in the Fig. 3d legend appear swapped.

concerns.quote: Fig. 3B : The scheme must be changed because this is transverse fluctuations
concerns.summary: The phase-fluctuation schematic shows longitudinal motion, whereas the observed effect is transverse.

concerns.quote: Fig. 3E : is it a fit ? From which data ?
concerns.summary: It is unclear whether the amplitude curve in Fig. 3e is a fit and which data it derives from.

concerns.quote: I find the results—though well executed—somewhat disappointing in terms of their physical significance. The interpretation could also be further developed.
concerns.summary: The physical significance of the results is limited and the interpretation underdeveloped.

concerns.quote: The wording in abstract and conclusions give the reader the impression that optical tunability is a unique property of JC-CDWs and there is no mention of the photoinduced modulation in twist angle
concerns.summary: The paper overstates the uniqueness of optical moiré tuning and omits prior work (Duncan et al., Nature 2025).

concerns.quote: In the caption it is mentioned that “I denotes the scattering intensity”, yet there is no intensity scale in the figure.
concerns.summary: Fig. 1b lacks a quantitative intensity scale.

concerns.quote: the formation of the JC-CDW from I-CDWs in different tellurium planes is not directly obvious.
concerns.summary: A real-space schematic of the monolayer and bilayer CDWs in different Te planes forming the JC-CDW is needed.

concerns.quote: As the polarization is only specified in the XRD methods section, I would like the authors to comment, if they observed a polarization dependence
concerns.summary: Pump polarization dependence should be checked and reported, along with whether the same polarization was used throughout; the rebuttal says an S-polarized pump was used in all measurements, whereas v1 Methods states a p-polarized tr-XRD pump.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: it is stated that the bilayer CDW is not detectable in UED experiments. This point is not further commented
concerns.summary: The reason the bilayer CDW cannot be detected in UED is not explained.

first_round.quote: I therefore recommend that the authors revise the manuscript and address the points above before it can be considered for publication in Nature Communications.
I find the results—though well executed—somewhat disappointing in terms of their physical significance. The interpretation could also be further developed.
I am convinced by the validity of the results and the balanced conclusions... I generally support publication after the authors have addressed the below comments

recommendations.note: The file starts at Version 0 at Nature Communications, with no transfer from another journal; only the Version 0 reports were used. No referee uses the scale terms, so all three levels are inferred. R1 says the issues 'prevent this referee from recommending publication' and asks for reorganization plus stronger justification of the topological-defect and amplitude/phase claims, which points to major revision. R2 is the least certain call. It gives no explicit verdict, questions the significance, calls the topological scenario 'naive', and says the paper is 'difficult to accept... unless the ref 4 has been published'. Its points are mostly addressable alternative explanations and clarifications, so major revision was chosen over reject, but a reject reading is defensible. R3's requests are small clarifications and figure fixes, so minor revision. All referees are individual reports; none co-signs another's report.
recommendations.label: contested
